newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Indian copper demand seen rising 50 pct by 2001.
newsitem.headline: Indian copper demand seen rising 50 pct by 2001.

text.p: India's demand for copper is likely to rise nearly 50 percent to 481,520 tonnes in the years 2000/01 from 321,080 tonnes in 1995/96, International Copper Study Group (ICSG) said.
In a brief communique giving some highlights of a survey of the Indian copper market, the Group said that demand should rise to a further 695,750 tonnes by the years 2005/06.

It said that electrical, electronics and telecommunication sectors are projected to consume 243,910 tonnes of copper in 2000/01 against 163,830 tonnes in 1995/96. Demand should rise further to 344,850 tonnes in 2005/06.
In order to meet growing demand, India expects to increase installed capacity to around 516,000 tonnes over the next five to 10 years, it said. It gave no figure for current capacity.
